title: Boss: the compose doctor
summary: A linter for compose files: missing images, broken dependencies, port clashes, cycles and health conditions that can never pass.

steps.title: Before anyone runs up
steps.body: Your team wants a check that runs in CI on every `compose.yaml`, so broken files fail fast with a clear message instead of a confusing error on someone's laptop. All three exercises read the same YAML subset (two-space indents; `services:` at 0, names at 2, keys at 4, list items or long-form `depends_on` names at 6, `condition:` at 8).

steps.title: Structural checks
prompt: Write `List<string> Validate(List<string> lines)` that reports, in this order:
1. for each service in file order: `SVC: needs image or build` if it has neither; then `SVC: depends on missing service 'X'` for each dependency that is not a service (in the order listed);

2. then, for each host port published by more than one service: `port P published by A and B` (services in file order; ports in order of first appearance; a mapping is `"HOST:CONTAINER"` or `"IP:HOST:CONTAINER"`).
Return `ok` alone if nothing is wrong.
solution: var services = new Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, List<string>>>();
if (indent == 0) { inServices = line == "services:"; svc = null; continue; }
if (indent == 2) { svc = line.TrimEnd(':'); services[svc] = new Dictionary<string, List<string>>(); key = null; }
List<string> Get(string s, string key) => services[s].TryGetValue(key, out var v) ? v : new List<string>();
if (!services[s].ContainsKey("image") && !services[s].ContainsKey("build")) problems.Add($"{s}: needs image or build");
if (!services.ContainsKey(name)) problems.Add($"{s}: depends on missing service '{name}'");
if (owners[port].Count > 1) problems.Add($"port {port} published by {string.Join(" and ", owners[port])}");
template: Dojo.Eq("valid file", new List<string> { "ok" }, Validate(new List<string> { "services:", "  api:", "    build: ./api", "    ports:", "      - \"8080:8080\"", "    depends_on:", "      - db", "  db:", "    image: postgres:17" }));
Dojo.Eq("missing image and dependency", new List<string> { "web: needs image or build", "web: depends on missing service 'apii'", "api: depends on missing service 'cache'" },

Validate(new List<string> { "services:", "  web:", "    ports:", "      - \"3000:3000\"", "    depends_on:", "      - apii", "  api:", "    build: ./api", "    depends_on:", "      db:", "        condition: service_healthy", "      cache:", "        condition: service_started", "  db:", "    image: postgres:17" }));
Dojo.Eq("port clash", new List<string> { "port 8080 published by api and admin" },

Validate(new List<string> { "services:", "  api:", "    build: ./api", "    ports:", "      - \"8080:8080\"", "      - \"9090:9090\"", "  admin:", "    image: adminer", "    ports:", "      - \"127.0.0.1:8080:8080\"" }));
hints: Parse into service → key → values first; long-form depends_on entries may carry a `|condition` suffix if you store it.
The host port is the second-to-last `:` part of a mapping.

steps.title: Order or cycle
steps.prompt: Write `string Order(List<string> lines)`: `start order: A, B, ...` using the alphabetically-first ready service each time, or `error: dependency cycle among A, B` (stuck services, sorted) when no service is ready but some remain. Dependencies on services that do not exist count as never ready (they will show up as stuck).
solution: var services = new Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, List<string>>>();
if (indent == 0) { inServices = line == "services:"; svc = null; continue; }
if (indent == 2) { svc = line.TrimEnd(':'); services[svc] = new Dictionary<string, List<string>>(); key = null; }
var deps = services.ToDictionary(kv => kv.Key, kv => kv.Value.TryGetValue("depends_on", out var d) ? d.Select(x => x.Split('|')[0]).ToList() : new List<string>());
string? next = deps.Keys.Where(s => !done.Contains(s) && deps[s].All(done.Contains)).OrderBy(s => s, StringComparer.Ordinal).FirstOrDefault();
return "error: dependency cycle among " + string.Join(", ", deps.Keys.Where(s => !done.Contains(s)).OrderBy(s => s, StringComparer.Ordinal));
template: Dojo.Eq("chain with long form", "start order: db, migrate, api, web", Order(new List<string> { "services:", "  web:", "    build: ./web", "    depends_on:", "      - api", "  api:", "    build: ./api", "    depends_on:", "      migrate:", "        condition: service_completed_successfully", "  migrate:", "    build: ./api", "    depends_on:", "      db:", "        condition: service_healthy", "  db:", "    image: postgres:17" }));

Dojo.Eq("three-way cycle", "error: dependency cycle among a, b, c", Order(new List<string> { "services:", "  a:", "    image: x", "    depends_on:", "      - b", "  b:", "    image: x", "    depends_on:", "      - c", "  c:", "    image: x", "    depends_on:", "      - a", "  d:", "    image: x" }));

steps.title: Health conditions that can never pass
prompt: Write `List<string> Waits(List<string> lines)` that explains what each service waits for, for every dependency, in file order of the dependent service and then listing order:
- short form, or `condition: service_started` → `A waits for B to start`
- `condition: service_healthy` → `A waits for B to be healthy`, **but** if B has no `healthcheck` key, instead: `error: A waits for B to be healthy, but B has no healthcheck`
- `condition: service_completed_successfully` → `A waits for B to finish successfully`
Return `no dependencies` alone when there are none.
solution: var services = new Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, List<string>>>();
if (indent == 0) { inServices = line == "services:"; svc = null; continue; }
if (indent == 2) { svc = line.TrimEnd(':'); services[svc] = new Dictionary<string, List<string>>(); key = null; }
string b = parts[0], condition = parts.Length > 1 ? parts[1] : "service_started";
result.Add(hasCheck ? $"{s} waits for {b} to be healthy" : $"error: {s} waits for {b} to be healthy, but {b} has no healthcheck");
else if (condition == "service_completed_successfully") result.Add($"{s} waits for {b} to finish successfully");
else result.Add($"{s} waits for {b} to start");
return result.Count == 0 ? new List<string> { "no dependencies" } : result;
template: Dojo.Eq("every kind of wait", new List<string> { "web waits for api to start", "api waits for db to be healthy", "error: api waits for redis to be healthy, but redis has no healthcheck", "api waits for migrate to finish successfully" }, Waits(dojoFile));
Dojo.Eq("no dependencies", new List<string> { "no dependencies" }, Waits(new List<string> { "services:", "  a:", "    image: x" }));
hints: Store long-form entries as `name|condition` while parsing (the `condition:` line at indent 8 follows its name).
A service has a healthcheck when its key dictionary contains `healthcheck`.
